description.narrative:
The main socio-environmental problems in Central America are related to the unsustainable management of natural resources, the scarcity and contamination of water, the reduction of biological diversity and the effects of climate change, which lead to the increasingly frequent occurrence of socio-natural disasters. It is necessary to generate technical environmental information from the perspective and realities of civil society, to be presented as evidence of the deterioration of the environment in the region and its consequences for human life and biodiversity in general. This information must have a technical-scientific quality, but also be pertinent to the realities of the local communities, considering gender roles, so that it reflects the difficulties and opportunities of these, thus contributing to regional and international debates in the search for joint solutions, which in turn, promote the collaboration of the different regional actors.
This project aims to contribute to the generation and dissemination of current socio-environmental information and equitable and inclusive proposals for the improvement of environmental public policies. To this end, it will focus on the development of the Natural Resources Observatory. This initiative seeks to create useful tools to systematise environmental information from the communities, analyse public policies on environmental issues of interest, generate evidence for advocacy and promote dialogue sharing the ideal of caring our common home.
